source: How this character moves. 'can_do' is what its body allows; 'tends_to' is its movement style. Style numbers were first measured from one reference video of the character dancing (Jimeng motion imitation, colour segmentation; hallucinated feet ignored). They are typical values, not limits: any dance may push past them as long as the motion stays within 'can_do' and keeps the style.

conventions.view: front; left/right are the character's own (its left arm is on the right of the screen)
conventions.arm_angle: deg between the arm (shoulder to hand) and straight down: 0 = hanging, 90 = straight out sideways, 180 = straight up; negative = swung across the front of the body
conventions.tilt: deg of the body's long axis from vertical, + = toward the character's left

arms.role: primary: they carry the choreography. Arm angular speed is about 10x the body's.
arms.nature: soft tubes that bend smoothly along their length (no sharp elbow); mitten hands keep their shape and can open or ball up

can_do.bend: anywhere along the arm, up to about 120 deg in total
poses_for_example: one arm up and bent over the head (wave)

tends_to.big_move: 100-170 deg in 0.3-0.4 s, then a short hold

usage_in_reference.symmetry: mostly asymmetric; the two arms move independently

constraints: raised arms pass in front of the hair, opening slightly outward
arms that cross the body pass in front of it

body.role: secondary: supports the arms; it tilts, turns and bobs as one soft egg (head and torso are one piece) and barely bends

can_do.bend: slight (the head and torso are one piece)

turn_deg.notes: estimated from how far the face moves across the body

squash_stretch.rule: squashes when low, stretches when high (correlation 0.68)

hair.role: secondary motion only, never driven directly
hair.notes: swings out on fast tilts and turns and settles back; makes the motion read as soft
constraints: keep the scalp still; the swing grows toward the ends of the hair

face.notes: expression changes with energy (smile, open mouth) in the reference. Out of scope for v1.

from_human.upper_arms: copy the dancer's upper-arm direction, full range including overhead and across the body
from_human.forearms: fold into the bend of the soft arm (hand ends near where the dancer's hand is, relative to the body)
from_human.torso_lean_side_twist: copy at reduced amplitude: tilt <= 16 deg, turn <= 40 deg
from_human.head: merged with the body: nods and tilts become small body tilts
from_human.legs_steps_kicks: no legs: in the reference a kick became a body tilt of ~14 deg plus a hair swing; steps become small bobs with squash; weight shifts become sideways shifts
from_human.hips: hip sway becomes sideways shift plus a small tilt

current_rig_gaps: raised arms are short next to the big hair, so overhead poses read less clearly than in the reference
an arm reaching over the head toward the other side passes in front of the face
coordination: arms lead, body follows: the body tends to lean toward the raised or moving arm about 0.5 s later (correlation 0.4)
hair follows the body about 0.24 s later
a fast sweep of an arm across the body comes with a body turn of 20-40 deg in the same direction
squash on the way down, stretch on the way up

bones.root: pivot at the base: body tilt / turn / lean, lift, squash
bones.arm_L_1..3, arm_R_1..3: soft arm chains (B-bones), parented to body_lower
bones.hair_1..3: spring chain down the back, parented to body_upper

signs_checked_by_render.arm_L_1.lean +: swings the left arm forward (in front of the body)

rig.driven_by: dancebuddy/retarget.py (quaternions per bone, from the dancer's torso frame and arm directions)
